Quantile-Quantile Graph of the Residuals

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_qq.Rd

Selects the graph of the quantile residuals of a fit against the quantiles of the standard normal distribution, with the line \(y = x\) and a pointwise band.

Usage

plot_qq(band = "order", level = 0.95, n_sim = 99, seed = NULL, legend = TRUE)

Arguments

band

"order" (the default) or "simulated".

level

The level of the band.

n_sim

The number of simulated responses of band = "simulated".

seed

A single number that seeds the randomization and the simulation, or NULL for the ambient state.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotQq object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

The quantile residual \(r_i = \Phi^{-1}(F(y_i; \hat\theta_i))\) is standard normal under a correct model (residuals.StatmodFit()), and the sorted residuals are drawn against \(\Phi^{-1}(p_i)\), with \(p_i\) from stats::ppoints(). With band = "order" the band at position \(i\) is the interval of level level of the \(i\)-th order statistic of \(n\) uniform variables, a \(\text{Beta}(i, n + 1 - i)\) variable, mapped by \(\Phi^{-1}\). With band = "simulated" the band is the pointwise interval of the sorted quantile residuals of n_sim responses drawn by simulate.StatmodFit(), each evaluated under the fitted parameters without refitting. For a discrete family the residuals are randomized, and seed makes them reproducible. The graph is not defined for a multivariate family.

See also

plot_worm(), diagnostics(), autoplot.StatmodFit()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(120, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_qq())

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_qq(band = "simulated", n_sim = 49,
                                      seed = 1))
